spine: Once upon a time, in Sunny Park in Ghana, there was a small silver robot named Pip who loved a wind-up toy mango.
Every day, Pip sat by the bench and wound the mango, watching it hop, while Ama swung on the swing or looked at leaves with her magnifier.
Until one day, the wind and the swing sent the toy mango hopping out of Pip's hands and under the flower bush.
Because of that, Pip searched under the bench, behind the tree and on the swing, but the toy stayed deep under the bush, and the sun began to sink toward the park gate.
Until finally, when the gate began to close, Pip walked to Ama and whispered, 'Help?' Ama smiled, knelt with her magnifier, and found the toy mango under the bush.
Ever since then, Pip and Ama play together in Sunny Park, and Pip always asks Ama to help him look before the gate closes.

setup.what: Pip winds his toy mango three times, holds it to his panel, and watches it hop, then reaches for it with both thin arms.
Pip kneels and stretches his thin arm under the flower bush, but cannot reach; the toy lies deep inside.
Ama calls gently from the swing: 'If the gate shuts, your mango stays all night, little friend.'
The park gate stands open at the left, its long shadow creeping toward the bench; it creaks as the sun sinks.
When Ama asks if he can climb the tree, Pip clicks his panel and says, 'No climb. No fly.'

beats.say: Pip winds his toy mango three times and sets it on the red earth. It hops.
Pip! The gate shuts at sunset. Mango and all.
Pip chases the mango, but.
A gust of wind takes it under the flower bush.
Pip kneels at the flower bush and stretches one thin arm under it.
Ama? Tick-tock?
Can you climb the tree and look, Pip?
No climb. No fly.
Pip tiptoes to the bench.
Pip peers under it.
Pip walks to the tree.
Pip peeks behind it.
Pip checks the swing.
Mango!
Pip picks up the yellow leaf beside the bush.
That one's a leaf-ball, Pip.
Pip looks at the gate, which creaks in the wind.
Pip looks at the gate as.
It swings shut.
Pip holds up the yellow leaf; it is not his mango.
Pip tiptoes to Ama at the swing.
Help?
Little friend! The gate can wait. I've been waiting for that one word all afternoon.
Ama takes up her magnifier.
Now we look-look. Was it a mango, or a leaf-ball, or a sneaky shoe?
Ama crouches at the flower bush and parts the leaves, magnifier at her eye.
Ama lifts the toy mango out of the flower bush.
Is this your little tick-tock thing, hiding with the flowers?
Boop! Mine, mine, mine.
Ama gives the toy mango to Pip.
Pip winds the toy mango three times.
Pip catches the toy mango as.
It hops off the path.
Three winds. Not two, not four. Every single time, little friend.
Pip gives Ama the yellow leaf.
Leaf-ball.
